findings.claim: The CLI exits before a briefing is written, so briefings triggered from CLI commands are lost.
The worker, which runs scheduled cycles, never registers the briefing writer, so scheduled runs get no briefing.
Writer registration uses one global slot, so one server's registration or removal silences another's.
The briefing drain only covers work that was in flight when the drain started, so briefings started during the drain are not waited for.
The web server does not drain briefings in flight before shutting down.

findings.claim: The Deep research 'working' line never ends when the underlying job dies, so the chat shows Ed working indefinitely.
The chosen corpus is reported to the person as applied, but it is not actually applied to the answer.
A Deep question asked of 'Your documents' runs web research instead of staying within the company's documents.

commit_note: Round one (23f4aef): 'Silent-failure blocked. Code and security passed with MEDIUMs.' No per-finding severity or reviewer attribution; the blocking HIGHs cannot be identified. Unresolved attribution.

findings.claim: A data file cut at the reading limit is profiled as if it were the whole file.
A refused Withdraw gives the person no indication that it was refused.
Excel cells shift to the wrong column when a preceding cell in the row is empty.
The profiler reports false dates (values that are not valid dates read as dates).
A partially successful multi-file upload is reported as all failed.
A file Ed could not read is reported as 'Added'.
Column kinds are inferred over-confidently.
A document's future expiry date survives a withdrawal, so the withdrawal does not take effect as an expiry.
A client learns a count of unreleased insights through the Withdraw flow.
